episodes.186632: A cold front and pre-frontal trough slowly crossing the area stalled over the Eastern Lake Ontario area. As the front stalled, a few bands of heavy rain developed along the front as an influx of moisture moved in ahead of and along the front.  This resulted in flash flooding overnight in southern Lewis County. Some of the highest rainfall amounts from this event, all from Lewis County, included 3.20 at Chases Lake; 3.14 at Croghan; and 2.11 near Glenfield.
episodes.186633: Strong cold air advection behind a secondary passing cold front prompted lake effect off of both lakes. This occurred as cooling temperatures aloft over the much warmer lake waters initiated a lake response. An approaching mid-level trough also helped contribute to the overall lake response. This setup resulted in waterspouts on Lake Erie near Lake Erie beach and near Westfield.
episodes.186717: A convective cloud line formed north of the lower Florida Keys, then propagated southward to the Atlantic-side waters.  A couple waterspouts were observed near developing rain showers along the cloud line.
episodes.189501: A surface trough lingered over and near the eastern Great Lakes during the late morning through early afternoon of the 7th as lake-effect rain showers streamed eastward from relatively-warm Lake Erie amidst a westerly mean low-level flow of sufficiently-cold/moist air and sufficient lake-induced instability. A waterspout formed along the low-level convergence/horizontal wind shear zone that accompanied a broken band of lake-effect rain showers that impacted northwest PA and far-northeast OH.
